response.sql: WITH per_order AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_rebtotal, AVG(rebrate / NULLIF(feerate, 0)) AS avg_ratio FROM fees WHERE rebrate >= 0.0005 GROUP BY orderslink), overall AS (SELECT p.*, AVG(avg_ratio) OVER () AS overall_mean FROM per_order p) SELECT orderslink, avg_rebtotal, avg_ratio, CASE WHEN overall_mean IS NOT NULL THEN avg_ratio / NULLIF(overall_mean, 0) END AS relative_ratio FROM overall ORDER BY relative_ratio DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;

assumptions.assumption: A feerate of 0 is treated as missing in the ratio (NULLIF), which avoids division by zero. An overall mean of 0 is also treated as missing, so the relative ratio is NULL.
Fee rows with a NULL orderslink are grouped together as one group and are not excluded. Rows with a NULL rebrate fail the >= 0.0005 filter and are dropped.
The overall mean is the unweighted mean of the per-order average ratios. Orders whose average ratio is NULL are ignored in that mean.
